issues.legal_issue: Entries in a statutory record of customs and practices do not, without evidence that the practices were exercised as rights, establish a customary right to quarry limestone for commercial purposes.
material_facts: The claim for a commercial quarrying right relied mainly on custom-sheets prepared during a cadastral survey under section 102 of the Bihar Tenancy Act, 1885.
The entries described taking stone for domestic or agricultural use and recorded fees or permits for removal for sale or other purposes.

The custom-sheets did not show that the recorded practices were exercised as a matter of right, and there was no evidence of specific instances of tenants quarrying limestone for the claimed purposes.
issues.conclusion: The custom-sheets did not establish the claimed customary right to quarry limestone for trade purposes.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 102 of the Bihar Tenancy Act, 1885, custom-sheets could have presumptive value as records of existing practices, but the revenue authorities were not determining whether those practices were ancient, certain, reasonable, and continuous. Accordingly, such entries alone had little value to prove a local custom, particularly where the recorded conditions indicated permissive use.

rule.if: customary_right_declaration_proceeding and custom_sheets_record_practices and (record_does_not_show_exercise_as_of_right or no_specific_instances_of_commercial_use)

predicates.customary_right_declaration_proceeding: A party sought a declaration of a right to exploit land or its resources based on local custom.
predicates.custom_sheets_record_practices: A survey or administrative record described local practices concerning use of land or its resources.
predicates.record_does_not_show_exercise_as_of_righ: The record described the practices but did not show that people exercised them as rights rather than by permission.
predicates.no_specific_instances_of_commercial_use: There was no evidence of specific instances in which the claimed commercial use had been exercised.

issues.definition: When a customary-right claim relies on records of practices that do not establish exercise as of right and lacks specific evidence of the claimed use, the commercial customary right is not established.

issues.legal_issue: A local custom granting an indeterminate class of persons a right to extract resources commercially from another's land is unenforceable when its exercise is unreasonable.
material_facts: The claimed right would allow tenants to quarry stone for trade from the hills or quarries in their villages, including through commercial operations using machinery.
The right was claimed for a class of tenants rather than as a right attached to a particular dominant tenement.
Exercising the claimed right to its full extent could destroy the subject matter and allow multiple tenants to work quarries simultaneously, creating a risk of breaches of the peace.
issues.conclusion: Even assuming that a local custom of commercial quarrying existed, it was unreasonable and could not be enforced by a court.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2 and 4 of the Indian Easements Act, 1882, distinguish easements, including certain profits à prendre, from a profit à prendre in gross; section 2 preserves customary rights, but such a right must satisfy the tests of a valid custom. A custom must be ancient, certain, and reasonable and is construed strictly when it derogates from general law. The Court relied on Lord Rivers v. Adams, Harris v. Earl of Chesterfield, Alfred F. Beckett Ltd. v. Lyons, Lutchhmeeput Singh v. Sadaulla Nushyo, and Arjun Kaibarta v. Manoranjan De Bhoumick; it distinguished Henry Goodman v. The Mayor and Free Burgesses of the Borough of Saltash and Mercer v. Denne.

rule.if: customary_profit_right_proceeding and right_benefits_indeterminate_class and commercial_extraction_from_another_land and (exercise_threatens_subject_matter_destruction or exercise_risks_conflict)

predicates.customary_profit_right_proceeding: A party sought to enforce a resource-taking right founded on local custom.
predicates.right_benefits_indeterminate_class: The claimed right would benefit an indeterminate class rather than being attached to a particular dominant tenement.
predicates.commercial_extraction_from_another_land: The claimed right involved commercial extraction of resources from land belonging to another.
predicates.exercise_threatens_subject_matter_destru: Exercising the right could tend to destroy the resource or other subject matter of the claimed right.
predicates.exercise_risks_conflict: The claimed right could allow competing users to exploit the same land simultaneously and create a risk of conflict.

issues.definition: A customary commercial extraction right benefiting an indeterminate class is unenforceable when its exercise threatens the subject matter or risks conflict.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant cannot obtain a declaration or possessory injunction over acquired land through rights derived from a former owner when those rights were extinguished on acquisition and the claimant had no transferred interest at the time of suit.
material_facts: Part of the land had been acquired for a railway, and possession had been taken by the acquiring authority.
The rights derived from the former landowner were extinguished in the acquired land when possession was taken.
The claimant's asserted interest in part of the acquired land derived from a lease granted to another company, and the conveyance to the claimant occurred after the suit was filed.
issues.conclusion: The claimant could not obtain a declaration of right or an injunction concerning the acquired land on the basis of the former owner's rights or the later transfer.
issues.legal_principle: On acquisition and taking of possession under the Land Acquisition Act, rights and encumbrances derived from the former owner in the acquired land were extinguished. A claimant could not enforce a derivative interest that had not been transferred to the claimant before the suit; the Court made no finding on whether the intervening lease had been terminated.

predicates.civil_declaration_or_injunction_proceedi: A party sought a declaration of rights or an injunction concerning land.
predicates.land_acquired_and_possession_taken: The land was acquired by a public authority and possession was taken.
predicates.claimant_right_derived_from_former_owner: The claimant relied on rights derived from the former owner of the acquired land.
predicates.claimant_transfer_postdated_suit: The transfer said to give the claimant an interest occurred after the claimant filed suit.

issues.definition: When acquired land is subject to a claim based on the former owner's rights or a transfer made after suit, the claim to that land is not maintainable.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant with established subsisting tenancy rights may protect possession of the tenanted land against unauthorized interference, but only for the land in which those rights subsist.
material_facts: The claimant had established tenancy rights in five plots derived from the landowner.
The claimant's possession of the relevant land was not challenged in the High Court.
Part of one plot had been acquired and was excluded from the protection granted.
The tenancy rights in the remaining plots had not been lawfully determined.
issues.conclusion: The claimant was entitled to protection against unauthorized interference with possession of the plots in which tenancy rights subsisted, excluding the acquired land, for so long as those rights were not lawfully determined.
issues.legal_principle: A tenant may protect possession of land in which the tenant has established subsisting rights against unauthorized disturbance. That protection does not extend to land whose rights were extinguished by acquisition, and it lasts only while the tenancy rights remain undetermined by lawful means.

rule.if: civil_possessory_injunction_proceeding and established_tenancy_interest and possession_not_disputed and tenancy_not_lawfully_determined and land_not_extinguished_by_acquisition

predicates.civil_possessory_injunction_proceeding: A party sought an injunction to protect possession of land.
predicates.established_tenancy_interest: The claimant established a tenancy interest in the land at issue.
predicates.possession_not_disputed: The claimant's possession of the land was not disputed in the relevant appeal.
predicates.tenancy_not_lawfully_determined: The tenancy rights had not been lawfully terminated or otherwise determined.
predicates.land_not_extinguished_by_acquisition: The land for which protection is sought was not land in which the claimant's rights had been extinguished by acquisition.

issues.definition: A tenant who establishes possession and an undetermined tenancy interest may obtain protection against unauthorized interference for land not excluded by acquisition.
